div.head: IV Eg 14
div.ab: Mid Anglum ic hæbbe gecoren ⁊ mine witan, hwæt seo steor beon mæge, gif ænig man mid ánbyrdnesse beginð oþþe mid ealle ofslyhð ænigne þara þe ymbe þás smeagunge bið ⁊ þæt dyrne orf ámeldað, oþþe þara ænigne þe on soðre gewitnesse bið ⁊ mid his soðe þæne unscyldigean ahret ⁊ þæne scyldigean rihtlice fordeð.

Mid Anglum ic hæbbe gecoren ⁊ mine witan, hwæt seo steor beon mæge, gif ænig man ánbyrdnysse beginð oððe mid ealle ofslyhð ænigne þara þe ymbe þas smeagunge bið ⁊ þæt dyrne orf ameldað, oððe þara ænigne þe on soðre gewitnesse bið, mid his soðe þæne unscyldigan ahret ⁊ ðæne scyldigan rihtlice fordeð.

Equidem cum Anglis inueni, quid ad correctionem illi proficere possit, qui, iracundie stimulis exagitatus uel audacia instigatus, quempiam illorum minatur aut penitus occiderit, qui sollicite pro iustitia et ueritate laborans, crimen furti uel quamlibet iniustitię culpam propalauerit suaque ueritatis rectitudine insontem liberauerit sontemque merito dampnauerit.

Mid Anglum ic hæbbe gecoren ⁊ mine witan, hwæt seo steor beon mæge, gif ænig man mid ánbyrdnysse beginð oððe mid ealle ofslyhð ænigne þara þe ymbe þas smeagunge bið ⁊ þæt dyrne orf ameldað, oððe þara ænigne þe on soðre gewitnesse bið [⁊] mid his soðe þæne unscyldigan ahret ⁊ ðæne scyldigan rihtlice fordeð.

Bei den Engländern habe ich und meine Witan entschieden, was die Strafe sein soll, wenn jemand Widerstand [gegen dies Gesetz] wagt oder gar einen von denen erschlägt, der um diese Untersuchung [bemüht] ist und das verheimlichte Vieh anmeldet, oder einen von denen, der bei wahrhafter Bezeugung steht und durch seine Wahrhaftigkeit den Unschuldigen rettet und den Schuldigen von Rechts wegen vernichtet.

Among the English, I and my witan have decided what the penalty is to be if anyone dares resistance [to this law] or even kills one of those who is [engaged] in this inquiry and reports the concealed cattle, or one of those who stands in true witness and by his truthfulness saves the innocent and justly destroys the guilty.

I and my councillors have determined what the penalty shall be among the English, if any man ventures to offer resistance or slays outright anyone who is engaged in this investigation and who gives notice of the concealed cattle, or anyone who is giving true witness and, by his veracity, saves the innocent and brings just doom upon the guilty.

Among the English, I and my councillors have decided what the punishment shall be, if any man offers resistance or goes to the length of slaying any one of those who are concerned in this investigation and who inform about concealed cattle, or any of those who give true witness and by their truthfulness save the innocent and lawfully bring destruction upon the guilty.

note.seg: Es scheint auf ein verlorenes Gesetz Eadgars angespielt. Dieses lehnte sich wohl an die Bestrafung des offenen Widerstands (s. d. Gl 3f.) gegen Gesetz (s. d. Gl 21ff.) und Polizei des 10. Jhs. allgemein, besonders gegen die Spurfolge oder Eintreibung der Kirchen- und Strafgelder, und drohte also Friedlosigkeit

There seems to be an allusion to a lost law of Eadgar. That law was probably modelled on the punishment of open resistance (see that word in Gl 3f.) to the law (see that word in Gl 21ff.) and public order of the 10th cent. in general, especially to the pursuit of the trail or the exaction of church dues and fines, and so threatened outlawry

‘beginnt’ Toller s. v. anbyrdnys; allein man verstehe nicht einen Ggs. zum Vollenden, sondern ‘sich zu verüben erdreistet’. Die Präposition mid, Deutschem und Englischem analog, find ich in Agsächs. Wbb. oder Grammatiken nicht; C liess sie fort, vielleicht weil selten

‘begins’ Toller s. v. anbyrdnys; but one should understand not a contrast with completing, but ‘has the audacity to commit’. The preposition mid, analogous to German and English usage, I do not find in A.-S. dictionaries or grammars; C omitted it, perhaps because it was rare
Dieselbe Steigerung des Verbrechens des Widerstands gegen Kirchengeldeintreiber s. d. Gl 1. 2
The same escalation of the crime of resistance against collectors of church dues: see that word in Gl 1. 2
Deutscher Syntax gemäss setzt Plural Schmid
Following German syntax, Schmid puts the plural
Richtig setzt Versio als Endzweck des Gesetzes, wie o. 2, 2 gesagt, Hinderung des Diebstahls
The Versio rightly gives as the ultimate aim of the law, as stated above 2, 2, the prevention of theft

Dies scheint anzuklingen ans Ehrlichkeitsversprechen; s. d. Gl 4; Anzeige 11. Die Gefahr, die Zeugen (s. d. Gl 14) bedroht, welche Viehräuber zur Strafe brachten, erzeugt jene Furcht, gegen die der Zeugeneid o. 6, 1 zielt

This seems to echo the promise of honesty; see that word in Gl 4; Anzeige 11. The danger threatening witnesses (see that word in Gl 14) who had brought cattle-thieves to punishment gives rise to the fear at which the witnesses’ oath above 6, 1 is aimed
Liebermann points out that such a provision is not found in the extant laws of Edgar. Presumably the reference is to a lost decree.
See Toller, Suppl. p. 73, s.v. beginnan, ii.
